newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie crops 45 pct seeded by May 20 - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie crops 45 pct seeded by May 20 - CWB.

text.p: Forty five percent of Canada's six major grain and oilseeds were seeded on the Prairies by Tuesday in line with the average seeding date, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst told Reuters.

"Being about half done by the 20th of May is not early by any means, it's about average for the Prairies. It would suggest that overall we've got fairly reasonable progress," CWB weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
Seventy-five percent of wheat, barley, canola, oats, flax and rye were seeded in Alberta by May 20 while Saskatchewan was 40 percent planted but Manitoba lagged behind, he said.
About half a million acres of Red River Valley crop land was submerged when southern Manitoba saw the highest flood of the river in 145 years earlier this month.
Flood waters remain high in Manitoba as the river slowly recedes.
While southern Manitoba need warm, drying weather, most of the rest of the Prairies need rain, Bullock said.
"Western parts of the Red River Valley and west almost entirely, I think the only exception would be maybe some of the areas of northeastern Saskatchewan, they all could use a rain," Bullock said.
"None of them are suffering, but they all could use a rain," he added.
Some areas of southern Alberta received little snow over the winter and were dry.
"They need rain there. It stretches right down into Montana and parts of western North Dakota as well," he said.
"There's a big drought pocket there that's building up and if that decides to grow over the summer that's more typical of western Canada," Bullock added.
